Thirty-six comments

This version of the tune is identical to an old New England version that I have. It has a dorian feel and I believe it should notated in E dorian rather than E minor.
However, there is a slightly different version in O’Neill (as Lannigan’s Ball) which is in E minor. This version is:

Eddie Duffy’s Lannigan’s Ball

There is a festival coming up in October (see current discussions) honouring the late Eddie Duffy (flute) and the late Mick Hoy (fiddle) of Fermanagh. So here’s Eddie’s version of Lannigan’s Ball as learned from fluter Rev. Gary Hastings in the early 80s. With no musical training, I am a paughle when it comes to keys. modes etc, so corrections are appreciated.

X: 1
T: Eddie Duffy’s Lannigan’s Ball
L: 1/8
M: 6/8
K: Em

Lanigan’s Ball, X:15

Verse 2:
Sure and it was me-self had free in-vi-ta-tions For all o‘ the boys an’ the girls I might ask;
In less than five min-utes I’d ftiends and re-la-tions All sing-ing as mer-ry as flies’round a cask.
Now kit-ty O’ har-ra, a nate lit-tle mil-li-er, Tipt me the wink and then asked me to call,
And whin I ar-rived_ with Tim-o-thy Gal-li-gan,_ Just In_ time_ for Lan-i-gan’s Ball.
Chorus:
Whack! fal, lal, fal, lal, tal, lad-ed-dy. Whack! tal, lal, fal, lal, tal, lad-ed-dy.
Whack! fal, lal, fal, la, tal, lad-ed-dy. Whack! hur-roo!- _for Lan-i-gan’s Ball.
Verse 3:
The_ boys were all me-ry, the girls were fris-ky, All drink-ing to-geth-er in co-ples and groups,
whin an ac-ci-dent hap-pend to Paddy O’ Raf-fer-ty, He stuck his fot through Miss Flan-i-gan’s hoops.
The cray-thur she fain-ted and roared, “Mil-lia mur-ther!” Then called for her friends_ and gath-ered thin all.
Tim Der-mod-y swore that he’d go __ no fur-ther, But have sat-is-fac-tion at Lan-i-gan’s Ball.
Chorus
Verse 4:
Oh, __ ar - rath, boys, __ but thin was the ’rup-tion; Me self got a wol-lop from Phek-im Mc-Coo.
Soon I re-plied to his nuts in-tro-duc-tion And we kicked up the div-il’s own phil-il-a-loo. __
Ca-sey, the pip-er he was near-ly stran-led; He squeezed up his bags, __ chan-ters and all.
The girls in their rib - bons all got en-tang-led And_ that put a stop_ in Lan-i-gan’s Ball.
Chorus
Verse 5:
In the midst of the row, __ Miss Ka-va-nagh faint-ed; Her face all the while was as red as the rose.
’The lad-ies de-clared her cheeks they were pain-ted, But she’d tak-en a drop__ too much, I sup-pose, __
Pad-dy Mc-Car-ty, so heart-y and a-ble, When he saw his dear col-leen stretched out in the hall,
He pulled the best leg from out un-der the ta-ble And_ brokw all the chi-ney at Lan-i-gan’s Ball.
Chorus(x2)

Eddie Duffy’s ‘Lannigan’s Ball’

From Hidden Fermanagh Vol. 2, as played by Jim McGrath, Seamus Quinn and Gabriel McArdle. The first part is very different to the usual first part of Lannigan’s Ball.
Eddie Duffy had this tune from his mentor, William Carroll, which takes the tune back to the mid C19th at least.

Lanigan’s Ball, X:21

Setting for mouth whistling.

This is my proposal to whistle it in the original session key. There is plenty of choice to do the changes of octave. This is therefore what I would do myself.

This is just to whistle along. I don’t think it would be good to do it as a solo being the main melodic instrument because in my opinion the change of octave at the end of the second part is a bit harsh.

Re: Lanigan’s Ball

This tune has been put to many uses over the centuries, preserving to a great degree, its shape.
Sometimes only fragments or parts of it were recycled, such as in the song
“Gin I were shot o’ her” whose 1st part is a version of “Fairly shot of her” but whose 2nd part is Lanigan’s ball’s 1st part.
https://thesession.org/tunes/10841
